home.name: Minseo Kim
home.subtitle: Researcher in Human–AI Interaction & Health Communication
home.motto: Make technology more human, especially when it matters most.
home.intro: I study how people interpret, trust, and make decisions with AI—especially in health contexts where uncertainty, emotion, and communication shape real choices.
home.paragraph: My research brings together Human–Computer Interaction, behavioral experiments, and AI-mediated health communication. I am particularly interested in what happens when an AI system presents uncertain information, and how we can design interactions that support more informed human judgment.
home.notice: Currently exploring Ph.D. opportunities for Fall 2027.

research.title: The questions behind my work
research.intro: I am interested in the human side of intelligent systems: how we understand their advice, and how their interfaces shape our judgments.
research.methodBody: Behavioral experiments · Human-centered design · Quantitative analysis · HCI research

projects.title: Communicating diagnostic uncertainty
projects.description: How should conversational AI communicate probabilities and empathy in early medical consultations?
projects.details: A controlled experiment (2 × 3, N = 180) examining probability information and empathy types, and their relationships with user evaluations.

projects.title: Fear anchoring in AI-assisted symptom assessment
projects.description: How do early AI-generated interpretations of symptoms influence subsequent judgments, even when more information becomes available?
projects.details: Studying anchoring, diagnostic uncertainty, and people’s ability to revise first impressions in AI-mediated health contexts.

projects.title: AI-powered pronunciation feedback
projects.description: Designed and developed a language-learning website that provides pronunciation feedback.
projects.details: Selected 1st place at Kwangwoon University’s 2024 graduation exhibition.

future.question: How can AI communicate uncertainty without amplifying anxiety?
future.explanation: Designing transparent, context-aware explanations that help people act on health information rather than fear it.

future.question: When should people rely on AI—and when should they reconsider?
future.explanation: Understanding trust calibration, anchoring, and revision of judgments when advice changes.

future.question: How can intelligent interfaces preserve human agency?
future.explanation: Exploring interaction designs that support reflective decision-making and meaningful user control.
